findings.title: --ignore-existing can falsely clear incomplete leftovers beyond the failure-report cap
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/retry.rs:118 — left_in_place derives its override set only from the capped failures sample, while retry_set at lines 98-102 uses the larger failed_paths set; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:280 caps failures at 64.
findings.predicted_failure: If more than 64 files leave incomplete destination copies during an --ignore-existing run, later paths retain --ignore-existing on retry and are skipped because their partials now exist. If the first 64 converge, the pass reports no failures and exits 0 while incomplete files remain.
findings.better_approach: Carry a typed left-in-place disposition for every retry path alongside failed_paths. If that identity must be truncated, preserve the unknown remainder as unretried instead of inferring behavior from the capped human-readable report.
